nodes.description: public string name; ERC20 token name set in constructor to KekwCoin
public string symbol; ERC20 token symbol set in constructor to KKW
public uint8 decimals; set to 18 in constructor
public uint256 _totalSupply; total token supply minted in constructor (10000 * 10**18)
mapping(address => uint) balances; token balances mutated by constructor, transfer and transferFrom
mapping(address => mapping(address => uint)) allowed; ERC20 allowance storage mutated by approve and transferFrom
KekwCoin constructor; sets metadata, mints _totalSupply to msg.sender and emits Transfer
totalSupply() view; returns _totalSupply minus balances[address(0)]
balanceOf(address tokenOwner) view; returns balances[tokenOwner]
allowance(address tokenOwner, address spender) view; returns allowed[tokenOwner][spender]
approve(address spender, uint tokens); writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] and emits Approval
transfer(address to, uint tokens); debits msg.sender, credits to using SafeMath and emits Transfer
transferFrom(address from, address to, uint tokens); moves balances and decrements allowance without reading the allowance value first
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint a, uint b) pure; returns a + b with require(c >= a) overflow check
SafeMath.safeSub(uint a, uint b) pure; returns a - b with require(b <= a) underflow check
SafeMath.safeMul(uint a, uint b) pure; returns a * b with require(a == 0 || c / a == b) overflow check
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint a, uint b) pure; returns a / b with require(b > 0) division-by-zero check
msg.sender; caller address used as balance/allowance owner in constructor, approve, transfer and transferFrom
Arithmetic c = a + b inside safeAdd; overflow guarded only by require(c >= a)
Arithmetic c = a - b inside safeSub; underflow guarded only by require(b <= a)
Arithmetic c = a * b inside safeMul; overflow guarded by require(a == 0 || c / a == b)
Arithmetic c = a / b inside safeDiv; zero-division guarded by require(b > 0)
uint tokens; amount argument of approve, transfer and transferFrom
address to; receiver argument of transfer and transferFrom
address from; debited account argument of transferFrom
address spender; allowance grantee argument of approve and allowance
address tokenOwner; queried owner argument of balanceOf and allowance
uint a; first operand of the SafeMath helper functions
uint b; second operand of the SafeMath helper functions
uint c; named return value holding the arithmetic result in each SafeMath helper

edges.reason: Constructor assigns the literal token name to state variable name
Constructor assigns the literal token symbol to state variable symbol
Constructor assigns decimals = 18 to state variable decimals
Constructor writes the initial supply into _totalSupply
Constructor writes _totalSupply into balances[msg.sender] (initial mint)
msg.sender is used as the minting beneficiary inside the constructor
totalSupply reads _totalSupply when computing the supply
totalSupply subtracts balances[address(0)] from _totalSupply
balanceOf returns the value stored in balances[tokenOwner]
allowance reads the nested allowed mapping
approve writes the granted amount into allowed[msg.sender][spender]
msg.sender is the allowance owner key written by approve
transfer reads and writes sender and receiver balances in the balances mapping
msg.sender is the debited account in transfer
transferFrom moves value between balances[from] and balances[to]
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender] without any allowance check
msg.sender indexes the spender slot of the allowance in transferFrom
transfer calls safeSub when debiting the sender balance
transfer calls safeAdd when crediting the receiver balance
transferFrom calls safeSub for both the balance and allowance decrements
transferFrom calls safeAdd when crediting the receiver balance
safeAdd performs the unchecked-by-compiler addition c = a + b on uint256
safeSub performs the subtraction c = a - b on uint256
safeMul performs the multiplication c = a * b on uint256
safeDiv performs the division c = a / b on uint256
approve stores the tokens argument as the allowance amount
transfer uses the tokens argument in safeSub and safeAdd
transferFrom uses the tokens argument for balances and allowance updates
transfer credits balances[to] with the transferred amount
transferFrom credits balances[to] with the transferred amount
transferFrom debits balances[from] and allowed[from][msg.sender]
approve uses spender as the allowance grantee key
allowance uses spender to index the nested allowance mapping
balanceOf uses tokenOwner to index the balances mapping
allowance uses tokenOwner as the outer allowance key
operand a feeds the addition inside safeAdd
operand a feeds the subtraction inside safeSub
operand a feeds the multiplication inside safeMul
operand a feeds the division inside safeDiv
operand b feeds the addition inside safeAdd
operand b feeds the subtraction inside safeSub
operand b feeds the multiplication inside safeMul
operand b feeds the division inside safeDiv
local result c is assigned by safeAdd and returned
local result c is assigned by safeSub and returned
local result c is assigned by safeMul and returned
local result c is assigned by safeDiv and returned

normalization_plan.reason: The tokens parameter is a transient argument bound to the transfer function frame and carries no independent state; fold it into the calling function node.
The to parameter is only meaningful within the transfer invocation and should be absorbed into the function node.
The from parameter exists solely as the debited account of transferFrom, so it merges into that function.
The spender parameter is a transient grantee argument of the approve call and should be merged into approve.
The tokenOwner parameter is a read-only query argument used by balanceOf and allowance and can be folded into the corresponding function node.
The operand a is a transient arithmetic input consumed by safeAdd and its siblings; normalize it into the safeAdd function node.
The operand b is a transient arithmetic input consumed by safeAdd and its siblings; normalize it into the safeAdd function node.
The named return variable c only materializes the result of the guarded arithmetic, so it merges into the arithmetic unsafe_operation node.
